findings.summary: The new os.Chmod runs on filepath.Dir(dst) even when the directory already existed, so it can chmod the current directory or fail with EPERM on directories like /tmp that the process doesn't own, breaking calls that worked before.

judge.reason: Names chmod on an existing directory like /tmp failing with EPERM, the same defect as b1.

findings.summary: The perm parameter is typed fs.FileMode but is used only as the directory mode, so a file-style mode like 0o644 creates a directory without the execute bit and os.Create then fails. It never affects the saved file, and extra variadic values are silently ignored.

judge.reason: The variadic-perm-ignored part is a known problem, and the perm-as-directory-mode complaint is a real design flaw. It does not describe the chmod-on-existing-dir bug.

findings.summary: TestSaveUploadedFileWithPermission saves to the bare path "permission_test", so it chmods and asserts on the working directory instead of testing directory creation. It also leaves the written file behind. The "Failed" test depends on permission denial and will fail when run as root.

judge.reason: The test chmods the working directory and leaves its file behind, and the Failed case breaks when run as root. These are real test defects.
